title: Duval County School Board, District 4
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school-tax rate, hire the superintendent (where appointed), approve school boundaries, curriculum policy and construction, and set district policies. Nonpartisan.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Rhodesia Butler
candidates.occupation: Area director, Boys & Girls Clubs of Northeast Florida; retired Duval County educator and administrator
candidates.background: Rhodesia Butler, 55, spent more than 21 years in Duval County Public Schools as a teacher, specialist, Early College coordinator, dean, assistant principal, principal and area director. She graduated from Stanton College Preparatory School and holds a master's in educational leadership from Jacksonville University, and has run a performing arts school and nonprofit for more than three decades.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

school_safety.summary: Butler names school safety and student behavior as her top issue but says she would address it through stronger behavior-intervention systems and more mentoring and student-support programs rather than added policing.
school_safety.quote: I will advocate for stronger behavior-intervention systems, increased access to mentoring and student-support programs

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide: Duval County School Board, District 4

teacher_pay.summary: Butler lists teacher and staff retention among her top three issues and says she would advocate for competitive salaries and meaningful professional development.
teacher_pay.quote: I will advocate for competitive salaries, meaningful professional development

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide: Duval County School Board, District 4

other_issues.title: Staffing and enrollment
other_issues.summary: Butler frames staffing as a fiscal-stewardship question tied to enrollment: 'you have to place teachers and principals where they need to be, but if you only have a certain amount of students, it just makes sense.'

sources.title: Who's running for Duval County School Board District 4? Meet the candidates

other_issues.title: College and career readiness
other_issues.summary: Butler says every student should graduate with a clear pathway to college, technical education, military service, entrepreneurship or the workforce.

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide: Duval County School Board, District 4

candidates.name: James Jacobs
candidates.occupation: Dean of students and athletic director, Duval Charter School at Westside
candidates.background: James 'Coach' Jacobs, 44, is dean of students, athletic director and a coach at a Jacksonville charter school, with earlier work as a paraprofessional, truancy officer, ESE assistant and physical education teacher. He holds a bachelor's in public safety management from Florida State College at Jacksonville and a master's in educational leadership from Nova Southeastern University, where he is pursuing a doctorate. He has previously run for Jacksonville City Council and for the school board.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

teacher_pay.summary: Jacobs' campaign website lists teacher pay as the first of three top priorities, calling for making competitive teacher pay a district priority and supporting a living wage for teachers and staff. He also lists higher stipends for part-time coaches and support for facilities and cafeteria employees.
teacher_pay.quote: Our educators deserve to be paid like the professionals they are.

school_safety.summary: Jacobs' campaign website calls for professional school-security solutions so that security staff handle safety and teachers can teach. It separately lists mental health as a priority, including more mental-health training and suicide-awareness education.
school_safety.quote: Safe schools, done the right way — let trained security professionals do their jobs, and let our teachers teach.

other_issues.title: Teacher retention and school culture
other_issues.summary: Jacobs says retention depends on creating a culture where teachers feel respected, supported and heard, with access to meaningful professional development.

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide: Duval County School Board, District 4

other_issues.title: Accessibility
other_issues.summary: Jacobs' campaign site commits him to being 'present, accessible, and accountable to the families of District 4.'

sources.title: Four Democrats face off in Duval School Board District 4 race. Who are they?

other_issues.title: School construction and closures
other_issues.summary: Jacobs says the district should be building schools rather than closing them, and lists renovating older schools to improve learning environments.

other_issues.title: Student meals and programming
other_issues.summary: Jacobs says he would protect free breakfast and lunch, expand after-school and summer programs for students with emotional-behavioral disabilities, and reinstate middle school sports teams.

candidates.name: Gracie Kearse-McCastler
candidates.occupation: Retired Duval County educator; former teacher and assistant principal
candidates.background: Gracie Bell Kearse-McCastler is a Jacksonville native who spent 33 years in Duval County Public Schools as a teacher and assistant principal. She and her three children attended District 4 public schools. She is running as a write-in candidate, so her name does not appear printed on the ballot.

teacher_pay.summary: Kearse-McCastler says teachers are overworked and underpaid and backs renewal of the district's one-mill property tax, which funds salaries, saying she would support it fully.

sources.title: Who's running for Duval County School Board District 4? Meet the candidates

taxes.summary: Asked about renewal of the district's one-mill local property tax for schools, Kearse-McCastler said she would support it fully rather than let the levy lapse.

sources.title: Who's running for Duval County School Board District 4? Meet the candidates

school_safety.summary: Kearse-McCastler raises the school-to-prison pipeline and high disciplinary referral rates among minority students as concerns, framing discipline as something to reduce rather than tighten.

sources.title: Who's running for Duval County School Board District 4? Meet the candidates

other_issues.title: Distribution of experienced teachers
other_issues.summary: Kearse-McCastler advocates a more equitable distribution of experienced educators across District 4 schools and says schools should keep showcasing their accomplishments to attract families.
